title: Ge/ZnS Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Differential Evolution Optimizer
scientific_hypothesis: Differential evolution global optimizer will escape local minima that gradient descent encountered in iteration_13, achieving higher target score by exploring thickness space more thoroughly while maintaining the three-cavity Fabry-Perot topology.
design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with computational optimization using global search rather than local gradient methods. Three cavities enable square passband profile with strong out-of-band blocking.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Air (24 layers total, alternating Ge/ZnS starting with Ge)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: conventional IR dielectric materials Ge and ZnS are depositable
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack with computational optimization principle from evidence
Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot enables square passband profile
expected_advantages: Global optimizer explores thickness space more thoroughly than gradient descent
May find better local minima than iteration_13's gradient-based result
Maintains proven Ge/ZnS material pair with high index contrast
known_risks: Differential evolution requires more function evaluations
May still converge to similar local minimum if landscape is rugged
Global search does not guarantee better solution
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer infrared bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate with alternating Ge and ZnS layers (Ge first, ZnS second, repeating for 24 total layers). Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. Initialize all layer thicknesses to 550 nm for Ge and 900 nm for ZnS (quarter-wave at ~4500 nm). Optimization bounds: 200-1500 nm for all layers. Use differential_evolution_thickness optimizer with population size 50, max generations 200. Objective: maximize weighted sum of mean transmittance in both passbands minus mean transmittance in both stopbands. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Changed optimizer from gradient_thickness (iteration_13) to differential_evolution_thickness to escape local minima and explore thickness space more globally while maintaining same 24-layer Ge/ZnS topology.
